title: US and China scale robotaxis as Korea readies 3,000-car push and rules
key_facts: Korea's Autonomous Driving Automobile Act lets robotaxi companies charge passengers in pilot zones once they get paid-transport authorization or a limited transport license.
Robotaxis in Korea still number only in the dozens; Autonomous A2Z reported 91 vehicles with operating permits at the end of 2025.

The government plans 200 Level 4 vehicles in demonstrations in Gwangju from the end of this year, and about 3,000 cars in five to six cities in 2027 for a little over 880 billion won; the budget is not finalized.
Waymo said in February it had about 3,000 robotaxis; Pony.ai's fleet reached 1,975 by the end of June and WeRide's passed 1,800 by the end of July.
A bill would require a safety manager in vehicles and separate operating permits from the national police; the industry calls this 'double regulation'.
A2Z signed an agreement with taxi associations in February, and Hyundai Motor takes part in a model that uses existing taxi licenses.
quote_evidence: Robotaxis in Korea still number only in the dozens.
The budget is not yet finalized and not all 3,000 will be paid robotaxis, but the direction is clear: moving beyond testing a small number of vehicles on fixed routes.
why_it_matters_hint: Korea is moving from a few test cars toward a fleet, which matters to passengers and taxi drivers.
notes: Read in full. The 3,000 figure is a government plan. Fleet counts are the article's own comparison, and it notes the counting standards differ.
